questions.question: Is WorkoutProgressionDefinition explicitly scoped to KEY_SESSION?
questions.answer: No. WorkoutProgressionStageDefinition (plan-catalog/src/PlanCatalog.Core/Models/WorkoutProgressionStageDefinition.cs) has no Role/SlotRole/StructuralRole field of any kind. SlotRole exists only on LayoutSlotDefinition (RUN_LAYOUT contract), a structurally separate artifact type. No validator ties a stage to a specific layout role. The architecture doc (Appsel_Master_Template_Catalog_Authoring_Process.md) describes the progression's declared scope generically as 'phase-relative stage order, candidate workout keys, exposure bounds, compression/extension behavior, runtime eligibility conditions, fallback stages' with no KEY_SESSION restriction anywhere in that description.
counterEvidence: Current v10 data: 5 of 7 stages target QUALITY-family workouts (the family compatible with KEY_SESSION per CandidatePublishGraphValidator.RoleCompatibleFamilies), which is the DATA PATTERN a reader could mistake for an explicit contract restriction.
questions.notes: The absence of a role field is itself the confirmed fact. Whether the CURRENT DATA is intended to represent 'KEY_SESSION only' content is a separate, unconfirmed question -- see A1-Q02.

questions.question: What do current v10 stage candidates actually target (family, phase, role-compatibility)?
questions.answer: 2 of 7 stages target the EASY family (FOUNDATION_EASY_BASE, TAPER_SHARPEN -> EASY_STANDARD); 5 of 7 target the QUALITY family (FARTLEK_INTRO, THRESHOLD_INTRO, TEN_K_SPECIFIC_INTRO, GOAL_PACE_REHEARSAL, CURRENT_FITNESS_SPECIFIC_REHEARSAL). ZERO stages target the LONG_RUN family. This directly contradicts a naive 'WorkoutProgressionDefinition only ever contains key-session-like candidates' framing -- EASY-family stages are already present and scheduled.
questions.notes: Per CandidatePublishGraphValidator.RoleCompatibleFamilies: KEY_SESSION accepts {QUALITY,RACE}; EASY_SUPPORT accepts {EASY}; LONG_RUN accepts {LONG_RUN}. Under this validator-encoded rule, all 7 v10 stages' candidates ARE family-compatible with either KEY_SESSION or EASY_SUPPORT -- never exclusively KEY_SESSION -- and none is compatible with LONG_RUN.

questions.question: How is the eligible-workout list (EligibleWorkoutKeys / EligibleWorkouts) actually used?
questions.answer: v10's actual INTERMEDIATE_MODIFIER v6 uses the exact-reference field EligibleWorkouts (VersionedCatalogReference list), NOT the legacy bare-string EligibleWorkoutKeys (IReadOnlySet<string>?) -- schema's oneOf forbids both being present simultaneously. For v10's schemaVersion>=2 ('exact') shape, WorkoutClosureResolver.ComputeExactClosureRefs computes candidateRefs (from stage.WorkoutCandidates) UNION eligibleRefs (from levelModifier.EligibleWorkouts) -- an ELIGIBILITY_FILTER/closure-union role, never a selection mechanism. For the legacy (schemaVersion 1) shape, EligibleWorkoutKeys is consulted in exactly 3 places: LevelModifierValidator (VALIDATION_ONLY -- existence check), TemplateCombinationValidator.ValidateEffectiveWorkoutSet (ELIGIBILITY_FILTER -- intersects with stage candidates for a non-empty-set check), and CatalogBundleAssembler's legacy-shape branch (ELIGIBILITY_FILTER -- filters candidateKeys before bundle assembly). Neither field is ever read to SELECT a single workout -- every consumer either validates existence or filters a set.
evidence: plan-catalog/src/PlanCatalog.Core/Models/LevelModifierDefinition.cs:18 (EligibleWorkoutKeys typed as IReadOnlySet<string>?, confirming it is a SET, not an ordered list -- order carries no semantic meaning)
plan-catalog/src/PlanCatalog.Infrastructure/Publishing/CatalogBundleAssembler.cs:85-98 (legacy branch, ELIGIBILITY_FILTER; exact branch uses WorkoutClosureResolver instead)
questions.notes: Because it is a SET (no order) and used only as a filter/whitelist, adding a second EASY-family or LONG_RUN-family workout to the eligible list would create NO ambiguity within this mechanism itself -- it would simply widen the closure. Ambiguity would only arise in a hypothetical FUTURE role-selection mechanism that does not yet exist (see A1-Q04).

questions.question: Is there an existing role-to-workout (or role-to-family) binding mechanism, versioned, deterministic, and used at runtime?
questions.answer: One mechanism exists, but it is authoring-tooling-side only, family-grained (not workout-key-grained), and NOT consumed by backend runtime at all. plan-catalog/src/PlanCatalog.Core/Validation/CandidatePublishGraphValidator.cs's private RoleCompatibleFamilies(SlotRole) switch statement (LONG_RUN->[LongRun], EASY_SUPPORT->[Easy], KEY_SESSION->[Quality,Race]) is used by the LAYOUT_SLOT_HAS_NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKOUT validation rule at candidate-publish time. It is: versioned only in the sense that it lives in versioned tooling source code (not a catalog artifact with its own key/version); deterministic (a pure switch expression); NOT used at runtime by the backend (RunningApp.Application has zero role-to-family logic anywhere -- confirmed by source search of CatalogRunLayoutSlots.cs / CatalogWeekSkeletonCalendarMaterializer.cs, which treat StructuralRole as an opaque string end-to-end).
evidence: backend/RunningApp.Application/RuntimeCatalog/Schedule/Materialization/CatalogRunLayoutSlots.cs (StructuralRole as opaque string, no family/role logic)
questions.notes: No role->exact-workout-key mechanism exists anywhere (only role->family, and only in Process A tooling). resolutionClass for 'a role-to-workout-KEY mechanism' specifically is NOT_FOUND.

mechanismTable.versioned: NO (tooling code, not a catalog artifact)

questions.question: What does the repository currently establish for EASY_SUPPORT?
questions.answer: EASY_SUPPORT is REPOSITORY_CONFIRMED as a layout-only role (RUN_LAYOUT_4D v2 slots). EASY_STANDARD (family=EASY) is REPOSITORY_CONFIRMED reachable from the v10 bundle AND is REPOSITORY_CONFIRMED as an actual stage candidate (FOUNDATION_EASY_BASE, TAPER_SHARPEN) -- unlike LONG_RUN, at least one EASY-family workout IS already stage-scheduled. However, the mapping 'EASY_SUPPORT (layout role) receives EASY_STANDARD (stage-produced workout)' is NOT explicitly encoded anywhere -- it is only an ARCHITECTURAL_INFERENCE from family-name similarity plus the validator's RoleCompatibleFamilies rule (which checks closure membership, not stage-to-slot binding). No other EASY-family workout is currently reachable. Workout progression DOES already control an EASY-family stage (2 of them) -- this is a repository fact, not an inference. Easy-run pace/distance is REPOSITORY_CONFIRMED deferred to prescription (WorkoutDefinition schema has no numeric dosage field at all). Workout IDENTITY itself (which exact key fills the slot) is NOT explicitly deferred anywhere -- it is simply unaddressed.
counterEvidence: No JSON field, schema property, or validator rule states 'EASY_SUPPORT slot <- EASY_STANDARD workout' as an explicit binding.
questions.currentRepositoryState: EASY_STANDARD is the only reachable EASY-family workout and IS already stage-scheduled (2 stages); no other EASY-family candidate exists in the closure.
questions.inferredMapping: EASY_SUPPORT (layout role) likely intended to receive EASY_STANDARD-sourced sessions, by family-name correspondence only
questions.ambiguity: LOW for family (only one EASY-family workout exists at all, so there is no competing candidate to be ambiguous about); HIGH for the underlying architectural QUESTION of whether role population should be stage-controlled, default-controlled, or something else -- since only 2 of the FOUNDATION/TAPER stages are EASY, while BUILD/RACE_SPECIFIC weeks have ZERO EASY-family stages, meaning the two EASY_SUPPORT slots in a BUILD/RACE_SPECIFIC week cannot come from any stage at all today.
questions.resolutionClassFinal: ARCHITECTURAL_INFERENCE for the family-level correspondence; PRODUCT_DECISION_REQUIRED for formalizing it

questions.question: What does the repository currently establish for LONG_RUN?
questions.answer: LONG_RUN is REPOSITORY_CONFIRMED as a layout-only role (RUN_LAYOUT_4D v2, exactly 1 slot). LONG_RUN_STANDARD (family=LONG_RUN) is REPOSITORY_CONFIRMED reachable from the v10 bundle, but ONLY via INTERMEDIATE_MODIFIER v6's eligibleWorkouts list -- MECHANICALLY_DERIVED (direct read): zero workout-progression stages in ten-k-workout-progression.v5.json reference LONG_RUN_STANDARD or any LONG_RUN-family key. 'LONG_RUN_PROGRESSION' does NOT exist anywhere in the active catalog/ directory as a workout artifact -- it exists only inside the tier-1 canonical Golden Fixture v3 generated PlanDocument (a DIFFERENT, distinct workout key with components, per an EXISTING, EXPLICIT governance decision in artifacts/audits/domain-wave1-schema-necessity-audit.md: 'the fixture's LONG_RUN_PROGRESSION key... is a distinct, non-substitutable workout key, not evidence for LONG_RUN_STANDARD itself'). No accepted decision requires phase-specific long-run workout identities. Long-run progression today is expressed ONLY through the phase-level PEAK_VOLUME_BANDS_V1 percentage/absolute-km bands (rule-pack-level, distance-only, no workout-key concept) -- confirmed no rule/policy artifact implies a long-run PACE curve, distance curve, or taper reduction tied to a workout-key change. LONG_RUN -> LONG_RUN_STANDARD is INFERRED ONLY (same reasoning as EASY_SUPPORT), and weaker, since LONG_RUN_STANDARD is not even stage-reachable.
evidence: plan-catalog/catalog/workout-progressions/ten-k-workout-progression.v5.json (zero references to LONG_RUN_STANDARD or any LONG_RUN-family key)

plan-catalog/docs/canonical/golden-fixture-v3/golden-10k-intermediate-4d-12w.v3.plandocument.json:1235 (workoutKey=LONG_RUN_PROGRESSION, family=LONG_RUN, MIXED prescription, has components incl. STEADY_FINISH)

answers.5_presentOnlyInExamplesHistoricalDeleted: Present only in the tier-1 canonical fixture (docs/canonical/golden-fixture-v3, an evidence/example artifact, not a catalog/ artifact) and in prose governance docs discussing it; also appears in the docs/archive/golden-fixture-v2 predecessor and in three audit documents explicitly discussing (not creating) it.
answers.9_explicitOrInferred: INFERRED_ONLY, and weaker than EASY_SUPPORT's inference since no stage reaches LONG_RUN_STANDARD at all
answers.10_finalClassification: GENUINE_DOCUMENTED_OPEN_GAP -- not simply intentional, not accidental, not undocumented. It IS documented (three separate audit artifacts explicitly discuss LONG_RUN_PROGRESSION and its non-substitutability for LONG_RUN_STANDARD), the decision to create it as a catalog artifact was explicitly deferred ('intentionally left as an open decision for a future, explicitly-scoped follow-up'), and it is not contradicted by any accepted decision. This is the most precise available characterization.

questions.question: Which bounded context owns role binding: Appsel.PlanCatalog or Appsel.PlanGeneration?
questions.answer: The only bounded-context split found (Appsel.PlanCatalog / Appsel.PlanGeneration) is explicitly labeled 'Onerilen bounded-context ayrimi' ('SUGGESTED bounded-context split') in Appsel_Master_Template_Catalog_Authoring_Process.md section 17 -- it is itself a recommendation, not an accepted, binding architecture decision. The document explicitly scopes itself to 'Process A' (Template Catalog Authoring) only and explicitly excludes 'Process B' (Runtime Template Assignment and Personalized Plan Generation) from its own coverage. No document assigns 'role binding' specifically to either side. What IS repository-confirmed: catalog declares available workout definitions and compatible candidates (Process A, versioned artifacts); runtime resolves phase allocation, calendar dates, and (per backend Phase 4F.1-4F.5) calendar-day assignment (Process B / RunningApp.Application). Nothing in either codebase currently claims ownership of 'assigning workout identity to a structural role' at all -- it is unowned, not merely unclear.
